newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity continues gains on West demand.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity continues gains on West demand.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading higher Friday based primarily on strong physical power prices in the U.S. West due to expected demand for air conditioning in the Southwest, industry sources said.
"It's market sentiment (pushing prices higher), they're going to need some cooling out West from electricity," said one New York-based futures trader.

As of 1210 EDT, June Palo Verde (PV) was trading up 40 cents at $20.00 following exchanges in a range of $19.80-20.05 per megawatt hour (MWh), while July was up 34 cents at $24.10 after trade as low as $24.00 per megawatt hour (MWh).
June California Oregon Border (COB) was trading up 30 cents at $14.65 after exchange as low as $14.50, while July was up 20 cents at $16.50 following trade as low as $16.30 per MWh.
NYMEX said that as of 1125 EDT, an estimated total of 17 COB and 39 PV contracts had traded.

Spot physical prices in the U.S. Northwest have been supported by cooler-than-normal spring weather creating some heating demand, while prices in the Southwest have been supported by air conditioning demand in hotter-than-normal temperatures, traders said.
Short-term electricity supplies across the West also have been constrained.
Hydropower availability in Northwest is reduced due to flood control measures in effect in British Columbia, and Bonneville Power Administration (BPA) is limiting daily offers for peak demand hours.
BPA said Friday it would continue to offer only off-peak power for Monday pre-schedulings, although some heavy-load hour volumes were available for Sunday.
As of 1210 EDT, June NYMEX Henry Hub natural gas futures were trading down 0.8 cents at $2.235 per million British thermal units.

About 4,000 megawatts (MW) of generating capacity in the Southwest is said to be currently offline for repairs or maintenance, although much of that capacity was expected to return to service later this month.
A 550 MW unit at the Jim Bridger coal-fired generating complex in Wyoming was expected to return to service Friday after being shut almost two weeks ago for repairs.

In the Pacific Northwest, temperatures would average near normal in the northeast to about two degrees Fahrenheit below normal southwest, with a chance of scattered precipitation this weekend, forecasters said.
In the Southwest, fair, dry weather is expected across the region with readings running near normal in the northeast to four degrees above normal in the southwest.
